name: Artificial Intelligence
description: GATE DA's AI: problem-solving as search, adversarial games, logic and reasoning under uncertainty.

nodes.name: Agents and problem formulation
nodes.desc: Agents and environments, states, actions, goal tests and path costs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe an agent and its environment and formulate a problem as states, actions, goal test and path cost.

nodes.name: Uninformed search
nodes.desc: Breadth-first, depth-first, uniform-cost, depth-limited and iterative deepening search.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run BFS, DFS, uniform-cost and iterative deepening search and compare their completeness and cost.

nodes.name: Heuristics
nodes.desc: Admissible and consistent heuristics, dominance and designing a heuristic by relaxation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to judge whether a heuristic is admissible or consistent and design one by relaxing the problem.

nodes.name: Greedy best-first and A*
nodes.desc: Greedy best-first search, A* and why an admissible heuristic makes A* optimal.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace greedy best-first search and A* on a graph and explain when A* returns an optimal path.

nodes.name: Local search
nodes.desc: Hill climbing, simulated annealing and the local maxima that trap them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply hill climbing and simulated annealing and explain local maxima, plateaus and restarts.

nodes.name: Adversarial search
nodes.desc: Game trees, minimax and alpha–beta pruning.
nodes.summary: You will be able to evaluate a game tree with minimax and prune it with alpha-beta, counting the nodes pruned.

nodes.name: Propositional logic for AI
nodes.desc: Knowledge bases, entailment, models and inference by truth tables.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent knowledge in propositional logic and decide entailment by model checking.

nodes.name: Resolution and normal forms
nodes.desc: CNF, resolution refutation and forward and backward chaining with Horn clauses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to convert sentences to CNF and prove entailment by resolution, forward chaining and backward chaining.

nodes.name: First-order logic
nodes.desc: Predicates, quantifiers, unification and inference in first-order logic.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write facts in first-order logic and apply unification and resolution to draw conclusions.

nodes.name: Acting under uncertainty
nodes.desc: Probability as degrees of belief, joint distributions and conditional independence.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason with degrees of belief using joint distributions and conditional independence.

nodes.name: Bayesian networks
nodes.desc: Network structure, the chain rule and exact inference by enumeration and variable elimination.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read independences from a Bayesian network and compute a posterior by enumeration or variable elimination.

nodes.name: Sampling and approximate inference
nodes.desc: Prior sampling, rejection sampling, likelihood weighting and Gibbs sampling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate probabilities in a Bayesian network by rejection sampling, likelihood weighting and Gibbs sampling.
